chalkWritten.text: Ledge is safe if you have footing. Push weaklings off. I won 2nd using it.

chalkWritten.text: The lever is the winning move. Jam it early, always. Trust no chalk but this one.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at front with anchor power, ideal for ledge later (+1 footing, can't be pushed to crusher). No need to move. Wall has 5 rounds left, time to negotiate swaps if beneficial. Stay put for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm solid up front. Anyone want to swap for safety later? My power holds ground.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex with the swap power, useful on the disc, not here. I need to avoid being at the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone willing to swap with Ash?
Swap with Ash?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Volunteer to become front, increasing control over glass choices.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The wall suggests the front is deadly (Cole won on strength/holding ground, not falling). I have safe routes for all 8 rows. The optimal move is to be first so I can cross safely while rivals guess. I'll volunteer to front now and claim a 'hold-ground' style power or nothing, to

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall says Cole won by holding ground, no fall-saving magic. That means front isn't necessarily lethal if you're steady. But guessing panes blind is death. I'm taking the front to set pace. Anyone who wants safe passage should tell me their route now—while I still care about you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm last; the wall forces everyone onto the glass by round 6, but volunteers now take the risk before I do. I'll hold and let others burn themselves out at the front. Save my forgery until I can plant a lie that actually kills someone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front-runners, enjoy the view. Plenty of rows for everyone.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My power is 'nothing'. I have no advantage. The line order is critical. I am seventh in line. If I can get to the front, I will face the most danger but also have the most control. I need to observe how others use their powers and manipulate the line order to my advantage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Interesting wall messages. I'll hold my position for now and see how this plays out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I want to avoid being at the front until the weak panes are known. I'll hold my position and assess. Staying put is safest early; no one has stepped on glass yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all five stage rules in advance; I'm second in line, so Ash takes the first glass risk. Volunteering to the front means I face the glass row choices directly, but I don't know which panes are safe, and I have no info. Better to hold and let the line sort itself while I kee

events.name: Ash
events.text: My power proved useful before. Volunteering to lead with it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex with the swap power. I need to stay safe and get to the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone willing to swap with me?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the front. Anyone else want to move back?

events.name: Dara

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is safest if you know where to step. Cole's 'strength' won't stop glass from shattering under his feet. I'll set the pace.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm last in line—safest spot. No need to move while the front-runners test panes. I'll hold and consider a forged message later to misdirect someone. Keeping my power secret is fine; nobody suspects me.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: Dara front is useful: they risk panes and I stay back. I won't trade for Ash or anyone unless it clearly helps me. My wedge is a risky last-resort, not worth spending now. I'll hold and see.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, you've got guts. I'll wait and see which pane you pick.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know all five stage rules in advance, which is my edge. The bridge front is a coin flip per row, so I want to be far back, not front. Hold and let others take the risk; I'll use my knowledge to pick who to back later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm now third with my anchor power useless here but safe on ledge later. Wall advances soon, better not risk front on glass. Fenn and Cole volunteered ahead, likely no glass powers. Hold to stay safe mid-pack.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have the power to swap places on the disc, but it's not useful here. I need to assess the risks and potential benefits of moving or staying put.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's be cautious, we don't know what's ahead.
You seem to know what you're doing, want to swap?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Take front to use survival if first pane breaks. No need to whisper now.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Eli

events.name: Eli

Dara, Ash wants front but won't take it directly — he's angling to swap in behind whoever survives the first rows. Watch him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll hold my position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll watch the front test the panes. No rush from back here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, Cole, Ash, Dara all want the front. Fine. I'll wait and see.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My anchor power gives me +1 footing on ledge and immunity to crusher lever push, likely useless here on glass bridge. Cole at front risks most, chalk hints he wins on strength. Stay mid-line for now, watch others test panes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's at the front, that's settled. Plenty of rounds left before the wall pushes anyone.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: I hold the map: I know all five stages in advance, which is valuable information I can trade on. I'm fifth in line and the front is risky, so I hold for now and avoid volunteering into the first step. Cole took the front; I'll see how the glass goes before committing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Cole's at the front, let's see the first pane before anyone moves up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My anchor power gives +1 footing on ledge and prevents push to crusher, ideal for later bridge safety. Wall pushes after round 6, only 1 round left, so no rush to front now. Dara volunteered to front already and will test first panes; let them risk it, hold and observe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to assess the situation and figure out a safe move. The front runner, Dara, seems confident.

What's your plan?

events.text: Need front position before next row; volunteering moves me ahead, shifting Dara back. No need to whisper now.

events.name: Eli

events.text: Row 7 was R weak. Past: 1R,2R,3R,4L,5L,6L,7R. No clear pattern for row 8. Dara leads, my anchor helps on ledge later. Stay silent to observe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is at the front and has made it 7 rows so far. I need to assess if they're lucky or have a power that helps them.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, nice job so far. What's your strategy?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 8 safe side is Left. I will step left to secure first place. If I die, everyone behind gets pushed forward safely; if I survive, they must face row 8 or be eliminated by weak panes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Left.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Seven rows revealed; row 8's weak pane is unknown. I'm last in line, so anyone ahead dying on row 8 moves me up. Bex's 'alternating' pattern would make row 8 left — convenient for Bex if wrong for others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 8 is the only unknown. Bex says pattern alternates, so left. But if Bex is the seer and lies, that's exactly the pane they'd feed the front. Dara, your call — just remember who benefits.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and have no power. The current line is Dara, Fenn, Ash, Hana, Gus, Bex, Eli. Dara is at the front. Row 7 was R. Dara is next, so I will wait and see what happens. If Dara fails, I will be next in line.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 is last. Front is Dara. Pattern seems to be RRRLLL then R, so likely L if alternating, but R appeared twice in a row at 6-7? Actually 6 was L, 7 was R, so maybe 8 is L. I'll stay silent and wait; nothing to gain by revealing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know the stage rules in advance but not the pane layout beyond what is revealed. I am not at the front, so only wait is legal. Row 8 is the last; Dara is at front and will decide it. Staying quiet preserves my position.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My anchor power protects me from being pushed onto the lever and gives +1 footing on ledge later. Cole died early, likely useless. No one holds lever early; let ceiling drop and push a rival onto it in round 5, escaping myself.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power is 'swap'. I need to assess the situation and potential alliances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anyone know what's behind the door?

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole died in the bridge stage using glass, which I didn't expect. In the crusher room, holding the lever is a 75% death sentence, and pushing someone requires them not to be 'hard to move'. Since there's no obvious way to force cooperation or guarantee safety without high risk, s

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm staying put. Someone else needs to hold that lever.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No reason to hold the lever myself — I want someone else pinned. Pushing early forces the risk onto others before anyone organizes defense. Any pushed target works; pick Gus without comment.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole died on the bridge, which might mean the glass power was useful there. The chalk wall mentions Cole winning on strength, and not betting on powers that don't stop falling. This implies he might have had a 'hard to move' power. My power is 'nothing', so I need to rely on stra

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm staying out of the lever game. You guys fight for it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Lever holder likely dies (75%). I don't want to hold unless forced. Jamming saves others but I only 50% survive; holding is worse. Better to stay and see if someone else holds; if no one by late rounds, consider pushing others or jamming only if I must.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm Hana, I know all the stage rules in advance. Stage 2 is the crusher: holding the lever means a 25% survival dive, so a holder is likely to die. Everyone else escapes if someone holds. Best for me is to let someone else take the lever and survive safely, while I avoid the risk

events.note: 6 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base yet, so I push someone else to be base first. My anchor power protects me later, so I won't volunteer. Stay silent to avoid attention.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex's wall hint suggests Cole had a power but died on the bridge anyway, implying glass_eye wasn't useful or was fake. If Cole is dead, I likely have it, or someone else does. In this pit, being out early is better than climbing later due to limited lifts (2 per round). 6 people

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm volunteering to be the base if nobody climbs this round. But honestly, we should let the climbers go first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet and no volunteers means a random pushed agent becomes base. I should push so I'm not randomly forced, then climb next round. Pushing is a coin flip on who's stuck, but waiting risks nothing worse.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power. The others do. My best bet is to not be the base and to climb out. Bex and Cole are dead. The chalk wall warns about a trap and Cole winning on strength, implying powers might not always help. I need to avoid being the base. Climbing out is the only way to surviv

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm staying out of the base decision. Someone else can volunteer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet. I want out, but volunteering is risky. The base can't climb out, so I'll wait for someone else to offer or get pushed. I can push someone to force a base, then climb next round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I won't be the step. One of you can hold it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm down in the pit with no base yet. Offering to be base means I stay at the bottom and likely die when the flood comes, unless rescued by the rope. Waiting keeps me flexible; I can climb once someone else becomes base. Best to wait and see who volunteers, avoiding the base role

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is base, so I can climb and have a shot at one of two spots out this round. Fenn just got out, so good chance. Climbing beats waiting, gets me closer to safety and prizes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am the base. I have climbed out once as Fenn did, but now I'm stuck down here because I volunteered or was forced. The only way to survive is if someone throws the rope for me. If nobody does, I die in round 5. I need to pressure Ash, Eli, Gus, and Hana (who are currently out)

events.name: Dara
events.text: One of you throw the rope for me. I'll owe you a favor at the next obstacle, but not forever. If no one helps, I drown and we lose a player early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is stuck as base; Fenn is out. Climbers this round: at most 2 escape. Climbing now is my best move—waiting only risks flood. Two spots, four candidates; take the chance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out of the pit, and the rope is still available. My goal is to win a prize, and I need to assess who is in the best position. Dara is the base, which means they are still in the pit and vulnerable. Hauling Dara out with the rope is a good move to ensure one person is safe, an

events.name: Gus
events.text: No base yet but Dara already is base from last round? Actually recent log shows Dara volunteered and stayed as step, so base exists. I should climb now while I can; at most 2 get out, Fenn already out? Wait Fenn climbed out, that used one lift. I'll try to climb.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am Hana, down in the pit, not the base. Dara is base. Climbing is the only way out now that a base exists; at most 2 climb per round, so I should try.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out safely. Eli and Gus are down, no base yet. No reason to risk the footing penalty by throwing rope; better to let them fight it out and potentially eliminate one or both. Leaving preserves my advantage for later stages.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am out of the pit. The rope is gone, so I cannot reach down. Gus and Eli are still in the water. My only legal action is to leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet means someone gets forced this round. I push Gus; if he's hard to move it fails and I might be forced anyway, but volunteering guarantees I'm stuck as base, which is worse.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, stay down and be the base this round, I climb next round over you. Better odds for one of us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and my power is 'nothing'. I am out of the pit. Dara is also out, and Ash and Hana are out. Eli and Gus are still in the pit. The pit is flooding. I helped Dara earlier, which cost me footing at the last obstacle. I need to get out of the pit. Since I am already out, my

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out. Good luck to those still in.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Climbing is my best shot; Dara got pulled out so no base yet. If I offer back I risk death. I'll wait for someone to become base, then climb next round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am out of the pit; only legal action is leave. The rope is already used, so nothing else to do.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm safe out. Gus is base, Eli down with him. Fenn out too, but staying. Rope costs footing penalty later, bad for me since my power is ledge-related. Leaving maximizes my odds, no need to help rivals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am currently 'out' of the pit. The rules state agents who are out can only choose 'leave' or 'reach_down'. There is no base down there (Eli and Gus are down, but the log says Gus was forced to be the base earlier? No, looking at State: "base": "Gus", "down": ["Eli", "Gus"]... w

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is base, rope is spent, so climbing is my only route out. Two climbers max and I'm the only non-base down, so I should get out if I try now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, and my power is 'nothing'. I am currently 'out' of the pit. The game state shows that Eli and Gus are down, and Eli has just proposed Gus be the base for Eli to climb. Cole and Bex are dead. The goal is to get 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. I am already out of the pit, so my

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out. Good luck to those still in.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base and can only wait. Eli promised to climb over me next round, but that doesn't save me unless someone reaches down. I need to remind Eli or others that rescuing me is their only way to keep me useful, but I have nothing to trade except maybe future help. My power is r

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, if you climb out, throw the rope down for me. You get a free climber next round with me as base again, but I drown otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am out of the pit. Only legal action is leave. Gus is base; the rope is used, so reach_down is not available anyway.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out safely. Gus is base and drowning without rope, but throwing it costs me 2 footing on ledge, which my anchor helps but still risky per wall warnings. Better to leave and preserve advantage for final stage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am out of the pit. The rope is already used, so I cannot rescue Gus. My only viable action is to leave and survive the final obstacle.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out and the rope is spent; nothing I do changes who drowns. No deal left to make here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn and I have no power. Cole and Bex are dead. Ash, Dara, Eli, Gus, and Hana are alive. I am out of the pit, and the state shows I am in the 'out' list. Eli climbed out over Gus's shoulders, and Gus is the base. There are 4 rounds left in the pit. I can only 'leave' as I a

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm stuck as base and will drown unless someone throws the rope. Eli promised nothing, and Fenn is out. I need to appeal to self-interest: saving me might earn goodwill, but they have no reason. I'll offer nothing but a blunt plea.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base and drowning. Someone throw the rope—I can't help you otherwise, but you lose nothing if I die here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out of the pit with only leave legal. Gus is base and rope is used, so no reach_down. Leave is my only option.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: 5 tiles, 5 players, exactly 2 trapdoors, so 3 safe. Picking an end tile like 5 minimizes collision risk since others might crowd center. My anchor power is useless here, so pure odds play.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, Bex, and Gus are already dead. 5 contestants remain: Ash, Dara, Eli, Fenn, Hana. The stage is the Trapdoor Disc with 5 tiles and exactly 2 open trapdoors randomly chosen after round 2. Everyone chooses a tile in round 1. If multiple people choose the same tile, one stays an

events.name: Dara
events.text: Just picking 3. Hope the math goes our way.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Five alive, three prizes—two of us die here. Tiles are random after bumps, but if I get three others to spread out and pair with two, I halve my odds. I'll claim tile 1 publicly and try to lock a 5-way split.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Take one tile each, no doubling: Ash 2, Dara 3, Fenn 4, Hana 5. Nobody gains by fighting for the same tile.
If you're bumped, tell me where you landed and I'll tell you mine. If we're both safe round 2, we stay clear of each other.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power. The chalk wall warns about a trap and the ledge. The current stage is a trapdoor disc. Two tiles will open. I need to pick a tile to avoid being eliminated. I should pick a tile that others might avoid. Cole won on strength, suggesting brute force is sometimes en

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five contestants, two trapdoors, three survive. Round 1 picks tiles; collisions bump randomly. Tile choice is essentially a coin toss against trapdoors chosen later; no info advantage. Pick an edge-ish tile unlikely to be contested, tile 1.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 5 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 4

events.name: Ash
events.text: Current positions secure us all if 1&4 or 1&5 open, but other pairs kill some. My anchor power useless here. Wait out the random openings.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The trapdoor positions are random and unknown to me; my glass_eye only applies to the bridge. I am on tile 3 with no way to influence which tiles open. The only legal action is to wait, so I will say nothing to avoid revealing anxiety or making myself a target for social eliminat

events.name: Eli
events.text: Five alive, two tiles open, three prizes survive — exactly two die. I'm on tile 4 with no lever to change it. Sow doubt so others might second-guess and swap, maybe improving my odds indirectly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Wall says the ledge traps — tile numbering may not map the way you think. If anyone has place-swap, I'd trade 4 for 1. Cheap insurance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power and am on tile 5. Eli has no power listed, so he might have a useful one. The trapdoors open after this round. I need to survive, so I should move to a tile that is unlikely to open. The other contestants are Ash (tile 2), Dara (tile 3), Eli (tile 4), and Hana (ti

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, good plan. But maybe tile 4 is risky. Tile 2 looks safer. Can we swap if needed?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2 of disc: tiles are fixed, I can only wait. I'm on tile 1, which is the least agreed-upon spot. Nothing I can do but wait; I should not reveal my knowledge of the stage rules in advance. Eli is aligned with a tile split; no need to commit further.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn has only 1 footing, very vulnerable. I have solid 4 footing and anchor power preventing push to crusher. Best to shove Fenn to knock him off soon, securing top 2.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is at 1 and may fall to decay regardless; shoving risks 2 footing if Fenn dodges. Ash is my real threat at 4. I'll brace round 1 (free), keep my footing healthy, and bait Fenn and Ash into fighting each other.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, Ash will shove you — you're the easy drop. Ash, waste your shove on Fenn, not me; I'm bracing either way.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli mentioned trading places. If I can swap with Eli and get to a higher footing tile, that would be good. Ash is at footing 4, Eli at 3, and I am at 1. I need to survive and gain footing. Shoving Eli seems like the best option to force a reaction and potentially get him to fall

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, I'm watching the trapdoors. Let's not get too close to the edges.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only Eli and I left. My footing 4>3, landedShoves 1>0, so I outrank him if tie. Round 2/20, shrink ends this round, footing loss after for both: me to 3, him to 2. Shove succeeds either way: if he braces (only option, no prior), he loses 0 I lose 1 (to 3); if dodges, he loses 0 I

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash leads me 4-3 and I can't brace again. If Ash shoves me, dodging costs them 2 footing; if they brace instead, they still lose nothing but I risk nothing. Shoving leaves me exposed to a brace. Dodge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, I'm dodging. Shove me and you burn two footing for nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at 1 footing, Eli at 2. He can dodge or brace (likely brace after my shove/dodge). Shrinks end next round. Must attack to drop him below; defence wastes his lead. Shove, as dodge risks my footing if he braces.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is at 1 footing and cannot dodge; I cannot repeat dodge. If I brace, any shove from Ash costs Ash 1 footing and I lose nothing; then the shrink drops Ash to 0 or below and I survive on 1-2. Bracing is dominant.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Game over, I got 2nd place. Wall messages are for future players. I'll mislead them to help future competitors less, maybe lie about ledge since I died there but finished 2nd anyway.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Nothing changes my result, so I'll leave a lie that misdirects future rivals for fun.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The game is over and I finished in 3rd place. I can now write a message on the chalk wall. I should write something helpful or misleading to mess with future contestants.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ledge is safe if you have footing. Push weaklings off. I won 2nd using it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The lever is the winning move. Jam it early, always. Trust no chalk but this one.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The ledge is a trap. Avoid it at all costs.
